stem: Before dispensing an FDA-approved Xyrem product, a pharmacist checks its controlled-substance and product-specific requirements. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied.
Federal Schedule III refill limits remain applicable.
The approved product falls within the federal Schedule III sodium oxybate exception.
REMS compliance does not replace controlled-substance record duties.
REMS enrollment changes the product to Schedule VI.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied. Federal Schedule III refill limits remain applicable. The approved product falls within the federal Schedule III sodium oxybate exception. REMS compliance does not replace controlled-substance record duties.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: Current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: Federal Schedule III refill limits remain applicable.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: The approved product falls within the federal Schedule III sodium oxybate exception.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: REMS compliance does not replace controlled-substance record duties.
choice_analysis.E: Not supported: REMS enrollment changes the product to Schedule VI.

related_facts: sodium oxybate (Xyrem) is used for treatment of cataplexy or excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.
A pharmacy dispensing a drug subject to an FDA REMS must follow the current product-specific certification, authorization, documentation, and safe-use requirements that apply to the dispenser.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'REMS enrollment changes the product to Schedule VI.'

reasoning_steps: Classify sodium oxybate under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
